title: constrain's floor waits the stage budget for the tester
intention: constrain's floor waits for the tester's run verb up to the stage's budget (STAGE_BUDGET_S, imported from cairn/machines/ticket/ticket.py), so a tester proof that runs longer than 180 s reads as its own verdict, not as unrunnable.
why: 4d597cac9f5d (7ae315843) makes bus.request's timeout bound an in-process handler. constrain asks the tester's run verb with timeout=180, and the tester's handler runs inside the bus process, so each proof over 180 s now raises TimeoutError and the floor records unrunnable. Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendelllinux: b0e65cf8a77e's floor ran 5 of 55 proofs over 180 s, the longest 1040.8 s.
traces_to: Law 7 (an unrunnable verdict is a record and must not claim a fault for a proof that ran green); Law 1 (one budget, imported, not copied); outline 3.3.4.3.
how: Orchestrator's ruling 2026-11-12, option (ii): _ask_tester imports STAGE_BUDGET_S from cairn.machines.ticket.ticket at call time and passes it as the request's timeout, in place of the literal 180. The proof runs a stub 'tester' on a scratch bus (wire_delivery, a reply by reply_to carrying body.record), patches bus_client.reach to a wrapper that scales every requested timeout by 0.001, and drives constrain._ask_once. It is red first against 7ae315843. Census of every other non-proof asker the rider now bounds, all fine: (a) inference_domain resolve, 30 s default, p99 1 s, the 3 over 30 s were one event on 2026-10-02; (b) codemother feedback (sail/reflection.py) and drain (skills/chart/live.py), 30 s default, handlers fast, the over-30 s cases (feedback 363 s, drain 77 s) were queueing behind a chart stage on her shim lock, which e4714e460e32 removes; (c) inference_domain infer, watch.py 60 s, max 29 s; (d) sail.py chart and verdict at 890 s and live.py at 120 s, answered at once by deferred gates (e4714e460e32) and settled by 0bcb816d6e9c; (e) tester's sealed is a post, not a request; the codemother commit verb has had no sender since f2b0d8105; (f) the get, calls, metrics, notices and notice-seen askers have max 7 s or less.

clauses.claim: a stub tester run slower than the old 180 s, with timeouts scaled by 0.001, comes back from _ask_once as the tester's green; on 7ae315843 it comes back unrunnable
the timeout constrain asks with is ticket.STAGE_BUDGET_S read at call time: patched to 1234.0, the ask carries 1234.0
a run past the scaled stage budget still comes back unrunnable, naming TimeoutError

decisions.text: D1: _ask_tester's timeout is STAGE_BUDGET_S, imported at call time.
D2: the proof, one tooth per clause, over a scratch bus with a stub tester and scaled timeouts.
